analysis.investment_thesis: Data Patterns is a recent IPO (listed December 2021) in defense electronics, exhibiting only four years of earnings history, negative operating cash flow in two of those four years, and a price that is simply grotesque by every quantitative measure I apply: P/E 79.4, P/B 12.72, EV/EBITDA 60, and a Graham Number of approximately INR 490 versus a market price of INR 3,494 — a 7× premium to intrinsic value. No margin of safety exists here; the investor is paying entirely for hoped-for future growth.
key_strengths: Zero financial debt (D/E 0.00) and an essentially unlevered balance sheet — the company cannot go bankrupt due to interest obligations, which is a meaningful distinction in a capital-intensive defense sector
Exceptional operating margins of 43% and revenue CAGR of 31.6% reflect genuine competitive strength in specialised defense and aerospace electronics with high barriers to replication
ROCE of 19.62% indicates the business earns well above its cost of capital on the assets it deploys
key_risks: Operating cash flow was negative in FY23 (−INR 17 Cr) and dramatically negative in FY25 (−INR 90 Cr) despite growing net profits — a dangerous divergence between reported earnings and actual cash generation, often indicating working capital strain from large contract-based revenues

Free cash flow was negative INR 196 Cr in FY25 — the company is consuming cash, not generating it, even at peak reported profitability; capex is rising rapidly (INR 106 Cr in FY25 vs INR 38 Cr in FY22)
Revenue of only INR 708 Cr makes this a small, concentrated business entirely dependent on Indian government defense procurement — any budget cycle slowdown or contract delay can devastate earnings
red_flags: P/E of 79.45 — more than 5× my maximum threshold of 15; the entire price is speculative expectation, not proven earning power
P/B of 12.72 — paying 12.7× net assets for a four-year-old public company is the definition of speculation, not investment
Graham Number ~INR 490 versus price INR 3,494: the stock must be purchased at one-seventh the current price before it qualifies as a value investment by my standards
OCF negative in 2 of 4 years — earnings are not being converted to cash, undermining the reliability of reported profits
Recent IPO (2021): by definition the seller (investment bank, promoters) chose the moment and price of this offering to maximise proceeds, not to benefit buyers
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Data Patterns operates an admirable business — specialised defense electronics with 43% operating margins and zero debt. I do not dispute the quality of what this company does. What I dispute, firmly and categorically, is the price being asked. At INR 3,494, Mr. Market is demanding that I pay 79× earnings, 12.7× book value, and 7× my calculated intrinsic value. This is not investment — it is speculation dressed in the language of growth. My method requires that I pay less than intrinsic value, not seven times more.

The cash flow data deepens my concern. A company reporting INR 222 Cr in net profit in FY25 whilst simultaneously generating negative INR 90 Cr in operating cash flow has a fundamental working capital problem — likely large receivables from government contracts that may be slow to collect. Free cash flow was negative INR 196 Cr in FY25. I will not pay a premium for profits that have not yet materialised as cash in the bank. The prudent investor waits — perhaps for a decade — until Mr. Market's enthusiasm for defense stocks moderates and this company's price approaches something defensible.
